premises: Cold deformation introduces residual tensile stress and high dislocation density in Q235 steel.
Residual tensile stress and high dislocation density serve as high-energy sites for anodic dissolution and film breakdown, accelerating localized pitting corrosion.
Stress-relief annealing reduces residual stresses and dislocation density introduced by cold deformation.
Reducing residual stress and dislocation density suppresses corrosion degradation, making behavior closer to untreated baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies to Q235 steel in 3.5 wt% NaCl at room temperature and 60°C.
